Report Description/// NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF AMERICA /// POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 06-11-2026 REPORT TIME: 0008 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: MAIN PASS 42 IMAGE DATE: 06-10-2026 IMAGE TIME: 1628 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL2C MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 10 METER LOCATION: 29°23'31" N/89°01'29" W AREA: 50.16 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 10.70 MILES EAST OF THE MAIN PASS CHANNEL IN LOUISIANA. IT WAS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH THE ANOMALY REFERENCED IN NOAA/NESDIS NRC#1464823, AS WELL AS NRC#1464855, WHICH REPORTED A LARGE UNKNOWN SHEEN IN THE MAIN PASS AREA. IT MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 25.8 NM IN LENGTH AND 1.5 NM AT ITS WIDEST POINT. THE ANOMALY EXHIBITED A BRIGHT RAINBOW SHEEN IN OPTICAL SATELLITE IMAGERY, WITH LARGE SEGMENTS OF SILVERY, WHITE, AND BROWNISH SHEENS THAT INDICATED POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. THE THICKEST POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED SOUTH OF THE ANOMALY'S CENTER POINT IN LONG, CONTINUOUS SLICKS. POSSIBLE THICKER OIL ALSO CONTINUED NORTHWEST OF THE CENTERPOINT IN SMALLER SEGMENTS. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE SE AT ROUGHLY 10 KNOTS. UNCERTAINTIES: A POINT SOURCE COULD NOT BE IDENTIFIED DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF MULTIPLE OIL WELLS AND FACILITIES WITHIN THE VICINITY OF THE ANOMALY. INTERMITTENT CLOUD COVER ALSO PREVENTED OBSERVATION IN LOCALIZED AREAS, WHICH COULD HAVE UNDERESTIMATED THE FULL EXTENT OF THE ANOMALY.

THE ANOMALY EXHIBITED A BRIGHT RAINBOW SHEEN IN OPTICAL SATELLITE IMAGERY, WITH LARGE SEGMENTS OF SILVERY, WHITE, AND BROWNISH SHEENS THAT INDICATED POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. THE THICKEST POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED SOUTH OF THE ANOMALY'S CENTER POINT IN LONG, CONTINUOUS SLICKS. POSSIBLE THICKER OIL ALSO CONTINUED NORTHWEST OF THE CENTERPOINT IN SMALLER SEGMENTS.
